The wing board

    Where the name comes from

    A town built with the tools on the sign.

    Wilkeson was a coal town, and a pick and a shovel is what it was built with.

    Settlers came looking for coal in the 1870s. By 1877 a Northern Pacific line was hauling it down to Tacoma; in 1885 the Wilkeson Coal and Coke Company lit its ovens; and the town was incorporated on 18 July 1909 — the same year the sandstone schoolhouse went up that still stands on the National Register.

    1,437 people lived here in 1910. Fire took much of the town that year and again in 1912, coke production stopped by 1937, and for a while people called Wilkeson a ghost town. It isn't one. Thirty beehive coke ovens still stand in the trees, the 1925 sandstone arch still marks the way in, and the brick block on Church Street still stops for lunch.
